answer:
FINAL HYPOTHESIS (natural-language, data-grounded):

"Higher socioeconomic status (SES) is associated with a higher probability of completing a bachelor's (BA) degree, and this positive association appears to differ along racial lines — the SES–degree-completion gradient is strongest among Black respondents, modest among White respondents, and negligible among Hispanic respondents after controls — although the formal race×SES moderation tests are not statistically significant, so the racial differences in the SES gradient are suggestive (strongest and clearest for Black respondents) but not conclusive.

Concretely, in a full-sample logistic regression of BA completion on SES (per 1-SD), race (White reference), and their interaction, adjusted for sex, ASVAB academic ability, class percentile, and family size: each 1-SD increase in SES multiplies the odds of degree completion by ~1.56 for Black respondents (95% CI 1.08–2.26, p=0.018), ~1.19 for White respondents (95% CI 0.99–1.43, p=0.063), and ~1.20 for Hispanic respondents (95% CI 0.77–1.89, p=0.42). Race-stratified models agree: Black OR=1.62 (1.09–2.43), White OR=1.26 (1.04–1.52), Hispanic OR=1.01 (0.62–1.65) after controls, with the Hispanic unadjusted OR (1.65) collapsing to ~1.0 once academic ability/percentile are controlled. However, the SES×race interaction is not statistically significant — likelihood-ratio test χ²(2)=1.75 (p=0.42) and joint Wald test χ²(2)=1.81 (p=0.40) — and the SES-tertile version agrees (LR χ²(4)=5.16, p=0.27). The moderation evidence is therefore directionally consistent with a stronger SES gradient for Black respondents but statistically weak, in large part because degree completion is rare among minority groups (Black: 28/2,113; Hispanic: 19/1,323), which limits power to detect a race-by-SES interaction."

WORKFLOW: Cleaned data (0 missing; 8,773 rows), standardized predictors; (1) primary full-sample logistic with SES×race interaction + controls (sex, ASVAB ability, class percentile, family size), reporting race-specific per-SD SES ORs with CIs, LR and Wald interaction tests; (2) race-stratified logits with/without controls (+ within-race standardized SES); (3) robustness: SES global-tertile binning with interaction, Firth penalized logistic for the rare outcome (236 events), and VIF collinearity check. All in executed script analysis_nls_ses.py. No causal claim; "affected by racial lines" treated as statistical moderation of an observational association.
